open_points.subject: upload stream and declared length
open_points.text: “reading the upload's stream, which `module:owner_interface` hands on unread with its declared length” and “An upload's bytes are handed on as the request's declared length and its unread stream”
open_points.question: Do the stream and declared length describe only the import file's bytes, or the entire HTTP request including multipart framing and other form fields?
options: The stream contains only the file part and the length, when present, is that part's declared length.
The stream is the entire request body and the length is the HTTP request Content-Length.
open_points.default_guess: Hand `migration_import` only the file-part stream and its optional part length, because A19 limits the import file's bytes rather than transport framing.

witness.initial: A valid owner session uploads an import file of exactly 52428800 bytes using a multipart form whose complete request is larger than 52428800 bytes.
events: The owner submits the upload form.
`owner_interface` extracts or forwards the unread stream and declared length.
outcomes: The file-part length is used, so the upload is accepted and its mapping is shown.
The request Content-Length is used, so the upload is refused before any file byte is read.
witness.observer: The owner sees either the mapping or an over-limit refusal.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: configuration item form checks
set_aside.text: “each well formed” and “Any check of an item or across items — presence, form ... — which are `configuration`'s”
set_aside.question: What exact form makes each text setting well formed, separately for store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential and service tokens?
options: Every set environment value is well-formed text; secrets have only the later byte-length and equality checks, and locations are rejected only by the later path-resolution checks.
Define an item-form check for locations and secrets, including which empty, NUL-containing or otherwise unrepresentable values are malformed.
Apply the host language or path library's implicit parsing rules.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat secrets as arbitrary unchanged text subject only to presence, UTF-8 byte length and distinctness; reject a location at the form stage only when it cannot be represented as a host path, leaving resolution and separation to the later path check.

witness.initial: All required variables and all four tokens are set; the store location contains a NUL character, and the backup key is shorter than 32 UTF-8 bytes.
events: `runtime_settings` returns both values unchanged as text.
`configuration` runs item-form checks before secret-length checks.
outcomes: The store location is malformed, so the start stops first naming the store location.
All text counts as well formed, so the later secret-length check stops first naming the backup key.
witness.observer: The host administrator sees a different first diagnostic.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: daily-backup look cadence
set_aside.text: “the minute look's 60 seconds is one that `instance_lifecycle` applies, calling `backups` at that interval” versus “At least once a minute, `capability:backups.run_daily_backup_if_due`”
set_aside.question: Must `instance_lifecycle` call the backup due-check at exactly 60-second intervals, or may it call more frequently provided no interval exceeds one minute?
options: Call at any cadence of at least once per minute, including more frequently.
set_aside.default_guess: Call once at start and then every imported 60 seconds, so the release constant has one observable meaning.

witness.initial: The process starts at 02:59:20 UTC and its initial look records that the date was seen before 03:00.
events: One implementation schedules subsequent looks every 60 seconds.
Another schedules them every 20 seconds, which is still at least once a minute.
outcomes: The exact-interval implementation first starts the backup at about 03:00:20.
The more-frequent implementation starts it at about 03:00:00.
witness.observer: The owner sees a different recorded newest-backup instant and a different snapshot boundary.
